  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34902v1</id>
    <title>Cross work induced by transformations on the symmetric group and related transformation semigroups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-26T06:24:11Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34902v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.34902v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We introduce a new permutation statistic, called the \emph{cross work}, on four important subsemigroups of the partial transformation semigroup $\mathcal{PT}_n$: the symmetric group $\mathcal{S}_n$, the semigroup of singular transformations $\mathrm{Sing}_n$, the symmetric inverse semigroup $\mathcal{I}_n$, and the semigroup $\mathcal{POI}_n$ of partial order-preserving injective transformations. The cross work is defined via local distance interactions between adjacent positions and their images. Fundamental invariance properties are established, including inversion invariance under a natural symmetry condition and a characterization of conjugations preserving the statistic. Using elementary combinatorial methods, we derive closed formulas for the total and average cross work on $\mathcal{S}_n$. We also determine the exact minimum and maximum values of the cross work, showing that the maximal value grows quadratically with $n$.</summary>
    <category term="math.CO" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34023v1</id>
    <title>The Symmetry of Differential Neural Tangent Kernel under the Orthogonal Group</title>
    <updated>2026-10-25T03:27:08Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34023v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.34023v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>The differential neural tangent kernel (DNTK) is a tool for analyzing the training dynamics of overparameterized physics informed neural networks. In this work, we investigate the symmetry of the infinite DNTK under an orthogonal group, for two layer and deep neural networks separately, based on the explicit expression of the DNTK and recursive formula, respectively. The results are for all activations with or without a bias term, and shed insight into the structure of the infinite width DNTK. Then we prove that the integral operators over the unit sphere induced by operators from the same group orbit share the spectrum, and their reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces differ only by an orthogonal transformation, and that the operator fixed DNTK exhibits zonal symmetry on the unit sphere for symmetric operators. Thus the eigenvalue decay rate of the associated integral operator can be derived for shallow networks with RePU activation and zero bias initialization.</summary>
    <category term="cs.LG" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33978v1</id>
    <title>On 2-Arc-Transitive Cayley Graphs of Nonabelian Characteristically Simple Groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-25T01:34:09Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33978v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.33978v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>The classification of symmetric Cayley graphs has attracted considerable attention. Results have been obtained for finite abelian groups and nonabelian simple groups. However, the problem remains open for finite nonabelian characteristically simple groups, although some results on normality for small valencies are known. In this paper, we determine the possible structures of automorphism groups $X$ of connected 2-arc-transitive Cayley graphs $Γ$ of $G\cong T^k$, where $T$ is a finite nonabelian simple group and $k\geqslant2$. In the quasiprimitive case, we prove that $G\unlhd X$, $Γ$ is complete, or $X$ is of product action type with restricted parameters. For the non-quasiprimitive case, we determine the possible structures of the quasiprimitive normal quotients of $Γ$.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33890v1</id>
    <title>The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle polynomials</title>
    <updated>2026-10-24T20:02:35Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33890v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.33890v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>This paper is the second in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. We focus here on the geometrical origins of these groups, as first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265. The spaces we are interested in are spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2πi}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2πi (k-1)}{k}}\}$. We show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. Moreover, we show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups $\mathcal{B}_n(k)$ inject into the larger braid groups $\mathcal{B}_{nk}$.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33692v1</id>
    <title>On the isomorphism problem of Cayley digraphs</title>
    <updated>2026-10-24T14:13:24Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33692v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.33692v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>A finite group $G$ is called a DCI-group provided any two Cayley digraphs $Cay(G,S)$ and $Cay(G,T)$ are isomorphic iff the two connection sets $S$ and $T$ are images of each other via automorphisms of the group $G$. Building on the vast literature on CI- and DCI-groups we present an updated list of possible DCI-groups. In addition, we give an alternative proof that does not rely on deep results from group theory. We also point out the three most important open problems related to the classification of DCI-groups.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33615v1</id>
    <title>Counterexamples to congruences in finite p-groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-24T11:32:48Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33615v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.33615v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Let $K$ be a conjugacy class of a finite $p$-group $G$. Héthelyi, Külshammer and the author asked whether the number of conjugacy classes contained in $KK^{-1}$ is always congruent to $1$ modulo $p-1$, and whether, dually, the number of irreducible constituents of $χ\overlineχ$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $p-1$ for every $χ\in\mathrm{Irr}(G)$. We construct a group of order $7^7$ for which both congruences fail.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33384v1</id>
    <title>Absolutely universal projective embeddings of long-root geometries of orthogonal type</title>
    <updated>2026-10-24T00:59:29Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33384v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.33384v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Let $G$ be a split Chevalley group of type $B_n$ ($n \geq 3$) or $D_n$ ($n \geq 4$), let $L$ be its Lie algebra and $Γ$ its long-root geometry, namely $Γ$ is the line-grassmannian of the polar space associated to $G$. It is well known that $L$ hosts a projective embedding of $Γ$, called the adjoint embedding, which realizes $Γ$ as a projective variety in the projective geometry of the underlying vector space of $L$. It is also known that $Γ$ admits the absolutely universal projective embedding, which is such that all projective embeddings of $Γ$ can be obtained from it as projections. When the field $F$ over which $G$ is defined is finite, the universal embedding of $Γ$ is just the same as the adjoint embedding. The same is not necessarily true when $F$ is infinite. Indeed, as we shall prove in this paper, the universal projective embedding of $Γ$ lives in a direct sum $K\oplus L$ for an $F$-vector space $K$, the dual of which is isomorphic to the derivation space $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ of $F$, which in general is non-trivial. Accordingly, the adjoint embedding of $Γ$ is universal if and only if $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ is trivial, namely $F$ is either perfect of positive characteristic or algebraic over its minimum subfield.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-10-24T00:59:29Z</published>
    <arxiv:primary_category term="math.GR"/>
    <author>
      <name>Antonio Pasini</name>
    </author>
  </entry>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33308v1</id>
    <title>A crystallographic quotient of the framed braid group and associated flat manifolds</title>
    <updated>2026-10-23T21:21:09Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33308v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.33308v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We study the quotient of the framed braid group $FB_n$ by the commutator subgroup of the framed pure braid group $FP_n$. We prove that $$ \frac{FB_n}{[FP_n,FP_n]}\cong\mathbb Z^n\rtimes\frac{B_n}{[P_n,P_n]}, $$ and, for $n\geq3$, that this quotient is a crystallographic group of dimension $n(n+1)/2$ with holonomy group $S_n$. We investigate its finite-order elements and conjugacy classes, prove that it has no elements of finite even order, and construct Bieberbach subgroups with prescribed finite $2$-group holonomy. Starting from suitable Bieberbach subgroups of $\frac{B_n}{[P_n,P_n]}$, we then construct Bieberbach subgroups of the framed quotient whose associated compact flat manifolds are torus bundles over the corresponding unframed flat manifolds. We describe these bundles through the generalized Calabi construction and determine their orientability, first Betti numbers, and the centers of their fundamental groups. As an application, we study a family with cyclic holonomy of odd order, obtaining a criterion for the existence of flat Kähler structures, and indicate how the same construction applies to cyclic holonomy of $2$-power order.</summary>

  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32775v1</id>
    <title>Large profinite genus and extensions in Bestvina-Brady groups</title>
    <updated>2026-10-23T15:24:44Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32775v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.32775v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We construct the first examples of uncountable families of residually finite duality groups of type $FP$, all of which have isomorphic profinite completions, while being pairwise not quasi-isometric. To establish these finiteness properties, we prove conjectures of Leary regarding groups of deck transformations of certain cubical branched covers being residually finite and virtually special. The main new tool is a strong separability result for Bestvina-Brady groups, allowing the extension of any finite quotient of many Bestvina-Brady subgroups to a finite quotient of the whole group. This gives a finite version of the congruence extension property, which we also establish for the same group pairs.</summary>
    <category term="math.GR" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
